# Release artifacts

`arduino-stc51-<version>.tar.bz2` is generated by `scripts/package-platform.ps1`. The platform archive and repository-built toolchains are published as versioned assets of the matching `v<version>` GitHub Release; the Boards Manager index references those immutable `releases/download/v<version>/...` URLs. Never replace a published asset in place. Any byte change requires a new version plus updated size and SHA-256 metadata.

Compiler and wrapper-host tools are separate, checksum-pinned dependencies and are not copied into the platform archive. Intended build hosts are Windows x64, Linux x86_64, macOS Apple Silicon (arm64, macOS 11+) and macOS Intel (x86_64, macOS 11+); qualification is tracked separately below.

This directory is not itself release evidence. The currently present macOS
`r1` archives predate the final combined SDCC patch and are **NOT QUALIFIED**;
they must not be published or entered into the current package index. The old
Boards Manager/release assets likewise do not represent the current 17-board
source tree or its experimental MCS251 C++ profiles. A host is listed as a build
target only after a fresh archive has been rebuilt, hash-pinned, and has passed
the required plain-C/C++ qualification matrix.

`sdcc-mcs251-linux-x86_64-<commit>-r<revision>.tar.bz2` is rebuilt in the pinned Debian 11 x86_64 environment with `scripts/build-linux-toolchain.sh` and a GLIBC 2.31 compatibility ceiling. The two `sdcc-mcs251-macos-<arch>-<commit>-r<revision>.tar.bz2` files are Apple Silicon and retained Intel flavours rebuilt with `scripts/build-macos-toolchain.sh` and a macOS 11.0 deployment target. The package revision changes whenever host packaging changes without changing the pinned compiler source. Exact provenance, byte sizes and SHA-256 values are recorded in `tools/toolchain-manifest.json`.
